desc:
Each interval [start, end) is half-open and covers every moment t with start ≤ t < end.

Find the longest continuous stretch of time in which every moment is covered by at least k intervals, and return its length. Return 0 if no moment is covered k times.

intervals = [[1, 4], [2, 6], [3, 5]], k = 2  ->  3
intervals = [[0, 3], [3, 6]],         k = 1  ->  6

In the first example the coverage is 1, 2, 3, 2, 1 on the unit pieces from time 1 to time 6, so the stretch [2, 5) is covered at least twice. In the second example the two intervals touch and together cover [0, 6) without a hole.
hints: The coverage count only changes at starts and ends. Between two consecutive event times it is constant.
Sort the distinct event times and compute the coverage of each piece between neighbouring times with a running sum of +1/-1 changes.

Walk through the pieces: if the coverage is at least k, add the piece length to the current run, otherwise reset the run to 0. Pieces are adjacent in time, so consecutive good pieces form one stretch. Track the best run.
editorial: Store the net change of the coverage for every distinct event time and sort the times. The coverage of the piece between times ti and ti+1 is the sum of all changes at times up to and including ti.

The pieces tile the range from the first to the last event without gaps, so a run of consecutive pieces with coverage ≥ k is one continuous stretch; two good pieces separated by a bad one are not. A single pass keeps the length of the current run and the best one. O(n log n) time for sorting, O(n) space.
